reviews.text: Andrew Haigh has woven...a fascinating story about the missed opportunities in every loving communication and the possibility of healing, through tolerance and forgiveness, wounds that are difficult to close. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Bonfil

reviews.text: It's a magical gift of a film. A haunting beauty worth seeing for anyone who has ever loved or longed.
reviews.author: Joonatan Itkonen

reviews.text: Even with some narrative flaws, Andrew Haigh's ghostly love story is overwhelmingly powerful.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: Featuring a quartet of excellent performances from the ensemble and a thoughtful, emotionally-rich screenplay, it's one of last year's very best films.
reviews.author: Jeff Beck

reviews.text: Warm, compassionate, and melancholic in equal measure, All of Us Strangers is perfect... Andrew Haigh tackles love, loss and loneliness whilst crafting an absorbing and fairly complex story.
reviews.author: Daniel Allen

reviews.text: All Of Us Strangers transcends the confines of traditional storytelling, offering a profound meditation on the nature of love, loss, and the enduring power of human connection.
reviews.author: Alex Valencia

reviews.text: “All of Us Strangers” transcends genres to create a strikingly penned, vividly painted drama that looks, sounds, and feels as singular as such a story can let it.
reviews.author: Ankit Ojha

reviews.text: Andrew Haigh's All of Us Strangers is a film that's nearly impossible to fully explain and just as impossible to stop thinking about. At the end of a recent screening, a friend turned to me and said, "The trailer didn't really prepare me for this!".
reviews.author: Stacey Yvonne

reviews.text: Adam’s distortion of his memories of his parents is sickening, which is disturbingly portrayed with a misplaced sweetness or, in the case of Adam’s relationship with Harry, humor.
reviews.author: Joshua Polanski

reviews.text: Haigh’s melan­choly, romantic ghost story, All of Us Strangers, was one of my favorite films last year and was unjustly overlooked by the Oscars.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: Surrealism and naturalism mingle to quietly shattering effect.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is altogether punitive in its despairing finish.
reviews.author: Cliff Froehlich

reviews.text: A poignant film about parents and partners, Andrew Haigh’s All of us Strangers is the most accomplished work of his career so far.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: A man in his late 50s meets his parents, who are twenty years younger. Taking up the idea of ​​a novel by the Japanese Taichi Yamada, the British filmmaker Andrew Haigh makes a very personal work. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: What Paul Mescal gets served, he delivers. He might miss in one instance or another, but when on call, he transcends expectations and draws great sympathy from the audience.
reviews.author: Jaylan Salah

reviews.text: Grief can be a powerful emotion that lingers long after the loss that spawned it. All of Us Strangers explores how regret colors one’s memories and allows one to fantasize about what might have been.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: The scene is jovial, lighthearted. Then it hits you like a wrecking ball, going for the tear ducts with the efficacy of a heat-seeking missile...
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: “All of Us Strangers” is “Jacob’s Ladder” (1990) with love instead of horror.
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: No movie from 2022 emotionally wiped me out as much as Charlotte Wells’ Aftersun, and no movie from 2023 emotionally wiped me out as much as Andrew Haigh’s All of Us Strangers.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: A poignant exploration of love, loss, and the healing power of connections that blends reality with fantasy through profound performances and a deeply resonant narrative.
reviews.author: Neil Soans

reviews.text: The biggest risk Haigh takes, remaining faithful to the fantastical component of the story, is what elevates the film... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Milagros Amondaray

reviews.text: Haigh does not deny the pain of departures and accentuates, to make it clear, the existentialism necessary to shoulder it. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Deserves merit for what it achieves, yes, but above all for what it avoids. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: This film encourages reflection on how our expectations shape the search for identity and interpersonal ties. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juan Pablo Russo

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is forever whiplashing us between the real and the imagined. It probably shouldn’t work, but the players are so astoundingly convincing that we find ourselves believing despite the craziness.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: It is transcendent stuff that puts a unique twist on gay romance from a deceptively innovative filmmaker.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: A heartbreaking and necessary look at loss, words never spoken, and love beyond this plane of existence. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juan Jose Cruz

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is heartbreaking. All of Us Strangers is heart healing. For those of us who have had to come out of the closet, it tells a truth rarely told.
reviews.author: Dave Giannini

reviews.text: A story about love, grief, nostalgia, and solitude. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alicia P. Ferreirós

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers displays a serene reflection on the perennial battle of the 'queer' collective against the prejudices imposed by heteronormativity. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Manu Yáñez

reviews.text: Andrew Haigh has composed a painful and relentless film about love -- familial, sentimental, and sexual -- that's romantic and reflective, but above all mysterious. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Javier Ocaña

reviews.text: The film doesn't always get it right when it tries to combine the romantic plot with the nostalgia of enduring a tragically interrupted childhood, but when it does, it hits the nail on the head, right in the middle of our hearts. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Randy Meeks

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is a remarkably profound film, and one that’ll cling to you tightly for days.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Andrew Haigh offers a precise and beautiful game of cinematic juggling at the very edge of all abysses. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: It’s a well-constructed and nuanced drama that drips with bold visual aplomb and a subtle mysticism akin to disorienting, dreamlike states... Indeed, it stands as something special in contemporary cinema.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Andrew Scott and Paul Mescal are the protagonists of a story in which love, in all its forms, transcends past, present and future, and even the afterlife. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Paula Arantzazu Ruiz

reviews.text: What makes this film work on many levels is Andrew Haigh’s direction. He possesses such a deft touch in conveying human experiences on screen and there is a moving beauty in its simplicity.
reviews.author: Liam Hanlon

reviews.text: One of the best films of 2024. An amazing screenplay that constantly keeps the audience guessing to where the film will go next. Andrew Scott and Paul Mescal are sensational.
reviews.author: David Griffiths

reviews.text: The strength of memory, and the fragility of it, are on display in “All of Us Strangers,” writer-director Andrew Haigh’s hauntingly tender drama about a writer stuck between his past and his potential future.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Writer-director Andrew Haigh touches upon the lonesomeness often associated with growing up gay as he builds a story about second chances and the power of love. Andrew Scott and Paul Mescal are phenomenal.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Restrained, nuanced and deeply affecting, this is one of the very best LGBT+ movies - or any movies for that matter - released in the last decade. This is a shattering story and in fact, I would wager, a truly perfect film.
reviews.author: Ben Turner

reviews.text: Scott and Mescal give career-best performances as two lovers clinging onto each other in an empty London apartment block. There are so many emotions and generational trauma in just a glance between the pair.
reviews.author: Amelia Harvey

reviews.text: The manner in which grief can embed itself into one’s life is given vivid, unnerving focus...Along with the explorations of love, loss and grief, Andrew Haigh also offers us a look inside the mind of someone whose hold on reality has become unshackled.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Andrew Haigh has crafted something special, brought achingly to life via four brilliant performances.
reviews.author: Robert Martin

reviews.text: ALL OF US STRANGERS [...] evokes the potency of storytelling when it collides with our memories of those who loved us, [demonstrating] the desire to determine the unknowable when combining our possible paths through life & those we lost along the way.
reviews.author: Jim Ross

reviews.text: This beautiful British movie about love, loneliness and the lingering after-effects of loss is well worth the track-down.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: It's terrific.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Andrew Haigh’s utterly magnificent All of Us Strangers summons such depth of feeling — and by such subtle magic — that you may feel blindsided by it. Do not operate heavy machinery after watching.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: It flies in its quieter and more subtle moments, lifting the lid on ideas of grief and the internalized guilt of growing up gay in an era when it was very difficult to be anything other than straight.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: I found heaps of resonance in All Of Us Strangers, yet watched in admiration rather than adoration, tremendously engaged but not enormously moved.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: I can’t think of another film that moved me the way this one did.
reviews.author: Chris Wasser

reviews.text: The universal theme of grief, particularly that around losing your parents, is dealt with delicately yet powerfully in All Of Us Strangers, the deeply moving latest project of British filmmaker Andrew Haigh.
reviews.author: Audrey Donohue

reviews.text: All Of Us Strangers is a mysterious, absorbing, slightly surreal film about love, in all its complexity, beauty and sadness.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: It’s an extraordinary film, both delicate and intense, a miniature that covers epic territory -- grief, loss, loneliness, fear and, above all, love.
reviews.author: Helen Hawkins

reviews.text: Being human is messy, and Haigh’s exquisite screenwriting captures a maelstrom of conflicting emotions...
reviews.author: Daily Express (UK) Staff

reviews.text: Many other writer-directors would have presented it as a tale of the supernatural. Here, though, it is earthly in the best sense: a love story of multiple kinds, marbled with loss.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: It would be incredibly easy for the film's delicate premise to go awry, but Haigh balances it all with a tonal mastery that pulls in viewers and makes them believe in magic — or something wildly close to it.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: Andrew Haigh thrusts the audience into an emotional gauntlet that even the most hardened heart will not weather.
reviews.author: Kat Hughes

reviews.text: Call it a writing exercise. Call it an acting exercise. Call it therapy. But you cannot find fault in the four lead performances, and very often the authenticity of their exchanges sank like a dagger in me.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: With only four real characters, All of Us Strangers generates a veritable furnace of feeling.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Inspired by Taichi Yamada’s 1987 novel Strangers, the director Andrew Haigh creates a raw and tender picture, with all four actors giving sensational performances.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is a mesmerising dreamscape of a film, full of tenderness, plus a haunting and incredibly poignant contemplation on grief, identity, loneliness and love. Stunning.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: The acting is off the scale. Scott, in particular, infuses his character with such vulnerability that you’ll want to reach into the screen and comfort him.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: A remarkable film, filled with wonder and fantasy.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Less a tragic nightmare than a beautiful, melancholic dream, All Of Us Strangers is one to keep close
reviews.author: Paul M. Bradshaw

reviews.text: Writer-director Andrew Haigh’s All of Us Strangers is part ghost story and part romance, and it feels like a warm hug.
reviews.author: Alex Heeney

reviews.text: Scott is fantastic, the supporting cast is excellent and Haigh's film-making has an elegance that makes simple, everyday observations feel profound. The results are both beautiful and haunting.
reviews.author: Matt Glasby

reviews.text: Haigh lends an eerie metaphysical dimension to the interiors, the trains and clubs that the film is set in. His writing is terse and pithy, working beautifully with human emotions...
reviews.author: Namrata Joshi

reviews.text: There's a moment that happens as a camera lens changes its focus, moving from foreground to background, where both parts of the image appear to soften and await resolution. That's the space British writer-director Andrew Haigh inhabits...
reviews.author: Cris Kennedy

reviews.text: After an impressive body of work, Andrew Haigh levels up even further, with a flawless film that reaches for the stars, and gets there. It aches and shimmers.
reviews.author: Alex Godfrey

reviews.text: Overall this is an affecting film, stimulating both emotionally and intellectually [and] imbued with a hallucinatory quality that suggests it’s all a dream, though one shot through with touches of grief-laden nightmare.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Although aspects of All of Us Strangers have a cheesy flavor, the raw honesty of the movie’s best moments propel the narrative through its less credible pitstops.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is a very sad movie. Director Andrew Haigh is careful to put a ray of hope inside that sadness, though.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Do not know if anyone has had time yet to scrutinize yesterday's lengthy list of British Academy of Film and Television Arts awards nominations -- better known as the BAFTAs -- but a serious film opening wide today received six of them.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: The sort of cinematic balm that not only touches your soul but takes up prime real estate.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: “All of Us Strangers” defies easy categorization in the usual fashion. But it’s also easy to place it in one category: that of really, really good movies.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: Haigh’s script shows a kind of genius for English humdrum understatement about the most wrenching matters. It’s an adaptation of a 1987 Japanese novel, Strangers by Taichi Yamada and radically improves upon it.
reviews.author: David Sexton

reviews.text: Filmed in muted tones with a quiet approach to even the most intense moments, All of Us Strangers doesn't need any loud antics or flashy gimmicks to be one of the most powerful films of the year.
reviews.author: Lisa Trifone

reviews.text: British writer-director Andrew Haigh (“45 Years,” “Weekend”) has made his best film yet, a hauntingly beautiful movie that’s simultaneously carnal and metaphysical.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: Fact and fiction are membrane-thin in writer-director Andrew Haigh’s fantastical enactment of grief.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: As for Scott and Mescal, their scenes together attain almost transcendental levels of subtle and unspoken understanding, and express the risk and pain involved in exposing oneself to love.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: [All of Us Strangers] is exquisitely acted by its four leads, especially Scott.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: If anything, Haigh is telling us the opposite: that the past sticks with us, for good and for ill. Which means there are dreams, and nightmares, that we never do wake up from.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: Inhabiting these space, the actors strike just the right level of nostalgia, reserve, pain, or release.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: Haigh has constructed a mystery that leans into the conventions of a horror story, but which remains hopeful and poignant until the credits roll.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: Where there is love, there is eternity. No matter who you are: queer, straight, mother, father, daughter, son, or lover – All of Us Strangers reaches out to embrace whatever notion of a soul you ascribe to… celestially beautiful.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: This plays as both a dream and nightmare, with some incredible performances. It's a very quiet and subtle experience, that dives into the complexities of human interactions, personal experiences and personal loneliness with such an emotional gravitas.
reviews.author: Elliott Collins

reviews.text: Sentimental with being cloying, serious without just the right touches of whimsy, joyful and yet knowing the sadness that comes with joy, All of Us Strangers is a deeply affective film.
reviews.author: Shelagh Rowan-Legg

reviews.text: In a contemporary tale for our time, writer-director Andrew Haigh pulls together an exceptional ensemble cast to take a deep dive into relationships as seen through the eyes of two disconnected people in need of comfort.
reviews.author: Martin Carr

reviews.text: The screenplay, by writer-director Andrew Haigh, is compelling, and very clever, with some surprising twists. I don't care for horror movies, but this one (which is equally a psychological drama) is an exceptional one.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Driven by such tender and thoughtful performances, All of Us Strangers is a healing, heartbreaking, and haunting look at the human condition that will stay with viewers long after they’ve left the theater.
reviews.author: Becca James

reviews.text: There are layers of secrets in All of Us Strangers that are not worth spoiling, but it's no secret that it's been a long time since a film has cast this kind of spell. It's worth holding onto.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: The loss of one’s parents at a young age brings unimaginable pain, and All of Us Strangers brings that to the fore in subtle yet powerful ways.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is beautiful to the bitter end.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: Like the best “Twilight Zone” episodes, “Strangers” fully embraces emotional sci-fi to leave a lasting impression.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: This drama might sound offbeat, but director Andrew Haigh's gentle, exploring tones make everything seem quite natural. It's a ghost story, perhaps, but there's more than one kind of ghost.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: What’s unquestionably real, though, is Adam’s pain, grief, and need for solace. In the end, Haig, whom I judge to be a director of generous spirit, doesn't deny him his comfort.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: A quietly stirring story of looking back in order to move forward.
reviews.author: Morgan Shaunette

reviews.text: If [Haigh's] previous films have felt like mere renderings of their scripts, this one is a genuinely cinematic experience.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is Andrew Haigh’s best work yet, combining all the elements that made his other films so successful. But it is also his most dense and inscrutable.
reviews.author: David Harris

reviews.text: Bring tissues. Delicate declarations of regrets, hopes, tenderness, and forgiveness pour off the screen.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: ...a fascinating character study anchored by the marvelous Andrew Scott.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: It's a chilly movie, but you really do care about all four characters.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: This is absolutely one of my favorite films for the entire year. A touching, soulful and haunting love story.
reviews.author: Manuel Betancourt

reviews.text: Elegant and startling and ambitiously spiritual...
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: It’s a happy marriage of form and content, in a film that’s wonderfully insightful about how emotions like grief and love can elongate time or compress it, or collapse it altogether.
reviews.author: Chris Klimek

reviews.text: Andrew Haigh’s tenderly haunting, impeccably-acted drama 'All of Us Strangers' takes the slow, steamy route to gay romance.
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: Packs an emotional punch strong enough to fell a person. Fraught conversations, longing and anxiety cut us to the core;  Haigh’s innovation creates a powerful, emotional sweep. Plan on recovery time.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: All four actors are brilliant, but Scott is key in how he negotiates an absurd and unsettling set of circumstances, gradually gaining confidence and self-awareness.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: In Haigh’s hands, the ghost story becomes a potent exploration of grief, and the impact it has on how we move through the world.
reviews.author: Alejandra Martinez

reviews.text: The final act will make you want to go back and watch it again, only to discover that the breadcrumb clues were there the entire time, from ominous apartment floor numbers to elevator reflections that create the effect of an infinity mirror.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: It can be watched as a fluid sort of reverie on roads and conversations not taken — heartbreaking ones. It can also be watched as an exercise in subtle visual excellence.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: Scott is in almost every frame of this movie, and his work is Oscar-worthy.
reviews.author: Odie Henderson

reviews.text: Director Andrew Haigh took the novel Strangers by Japanese writer Taichi Yamada and retold it as a love story between two men devastated by loneliness. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Aglaia Berlutti

reviews.text: Writer-director Andrew Haigh’s All of Us Strangers – an achingly beautiful meditation on love and grief – is the best film of the year and one of the decade’s absolute finest.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is a supernatural family drama, but it isn’t an “I see dead people” rehash. It is an intimate, haunting film that comforts and aches in equal measure.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: If there’s an absence of conflict, there’s great emotional power to the fantasy that Adam enjoys with his mom and dad.
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: Andrew Haigh’s newest film is an unusual and unforgettable cinematic masterpiece.
reviews.author: Peg Aloi

reviews.text: This is intelligent, punch-in-the-gut filmmaking at its finest.
reviews.author: Brian Bromberger

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is a melancholy, bittersweet and beautiful film about grief, loss and trying to connect with others.
reviews.author: Beth Accomando

reviews.text: Haigh captures the theme of loss, loneliness & love with such a piercing emotional impact. Scott delivers a career-best performance as the soulful hero teetering between dreams and reality.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: Andrew Haigh’s latest is pure poetry and a heartfelt tale of loss and healing. It pulls together some of the rawest, most hard-hitting scenes of drama ever put on film. One of the year’s very, very best, and it deserves space in your heart and mind.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: ALL OF US STRANGERS is without question one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: The romance is steamy enough—Scott and Mescal forge a chemistry that is both emotionally vulnerable and unbearably sexy—but Scott achieves a remarkable transformation in the scenes at home.
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers Kinda broke me. A surreal and Trippy experience that felt like a truck crashing right into me and breaking me down once I started to dive deep into it afterwards.
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Haigh has a real gift for things at once very basic to human experience and not at all easy to capture onscreen.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: The magical realism of All of Us Strangers in some ways feels like a kind of queer exorcism, a wistful exploration of family dynamics and chosen families that will be readily familiar to an LGBT audience.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Haigh knows how to build towering moments of human drama from the tiniest foundations. And he mostly pulls off such a feat again in this tale of grief and generational pain.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: An emotionally powerful film that represents a contemporary queer take on Field of Dreams
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Offers delight and devastation, with an ending that will haunt you with the necessity of connection (shades of E. M. Forster), and power of love.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: A fascinating and touching narrative that will stir the soul.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: What cinches this daring perspective is actor Andrew Scott’s phenomenal characterization as a weakling who grapples with gradual self-awareness.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: The fantastical premise is a delivery method for an intimate character study that is well acted but otherwise a bit too familiar.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Though fantasy predominates, the ultimate result is reality, the reality of wishful thinking and a desire for closure.
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: A transcendental and mysterious exploration of love, grief, acceptance, and human connection. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: Paul Mescal’s character injects a lot of energy into both the film and Adam’s life. He and Andrew Scott have wonderful onscreen chemistry together. The film could also work as a therapeutic tool for dealing with trauma.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: Tender but bruising, All of Us Strangers is an absolute marvel, the kind of movie that leaves a mark on you for weeks.
reviews.author: Kimber Myers

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers never veers into the sentimental or manipulative, offering an unflinching universal narrative of the costs of hiding from ourselves and the world.
reviews.author: Ana Yorke

reviews.text: A mystical, murky descent into an alternate world of sorts that sometimes works and sometimes doesn't.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Andrew Haigh has firm control of this artful story, spinning a tale of grief and love and building to a spellbinding, life-affirming, poetically transfixing, tear-inducing climax
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: “All of Us Strangers” is, in a way, a culmination of Haigh’s prior three movies, featuring, as it does, a burgeoning gay relationship (Weekend), a heterosexual marriage (45 Years) and a child’s yearning for a family ripped away from him (Lean on Pete).
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: But it’s those, “What ifs?” that make All of Us Strangers essential. It feeds upon dreams and nightmares alike, producing haunting, unavoidable truths about the human condition in the process.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: A quiet, affecting movie about one man reaching out for human connection.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: With its incredibly moving, cathartic narrative, All of Us Strangers is a film that will stick with viewers long after they're done watching it.
reviews.author: Audrey Fox

reviews.text: This small, simple film is the unexpected sweetheart of the holiday season and it’s a must-see. It’s my favorite film of 2023... it will be hard to beat. It’s weepy and emotional, but in that, it’s a beautifully touching experience.
reviews.author: Kimberly Pierce

reviews.text: A haunting meditation on how we can connect.
reviews.author: Bob Mondello

reviews.text: Andrew Haigh's movie is a magical experience exploring universal fears – grief, isolation, loneliness, fear of not being loved – while creating an incredibly touching, personal story about queer trauma.
reviews.author: Mireia Mullor

reviews.text: Scott is the one subtly shouldering the storytelling. Even if you’ve seen his theater work or some of his deeper cuts on British TV, his work in this moving tale about the power of love still feels like a revelation.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: This is an intriguing, increasingly mystifying rabbit hole disguised as a romantic drama, with all the sensuous pleasures the genre suggests.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: The film becomes more heart-wrenching as it moves on. How could it not? But every imagined scene remains full of authentic emotion.
reviews.author: Caryn James

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is a beautiful, poignant film that explores grief in a raw, realistic way. It’s also the kind of story that feels designed just to hurt you.
reviews.author: Lissete Lanuza Sáenz

reviews.text: Final plot twist notwithstanding, Andrew Haigh’s All of Us Strangers is a cathartic and brilliantly-acted melodrama.
reviews.author: Marisa Carpico

reviews.text: The intimacy feels authentic, and so does the accompanying guilt and regret. The result is quietly powerful without resorting to heavy-handed sentimentality.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: The world is so claustrophobically warped to fit the specifics of Adam’s unhappiness, as if it’s trying to justify his solitude. I started hoping for a reveal that what we’ve been watching is the script Adam was writing.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Andrew Haigh's ghastly All of Us Strangers is a solid melodrama held by its mighty ensemble carried by Andrew Scott's incredible performance.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: A film that will make you reflect on your own lives; about your parents, and about the time you spend with your loved ones. It's a perfectly acted film, elegantly directed and photographed, featuring a mesmerizing soundtrack. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Haigh beautifully handles the narrative progressions to ensure he doesn't have to jump through hoops distracting us from a truth hidden in plain sight. He knows how to use his script to prevent us from asking questions, but it never feels manipulative.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: This potentially maudlin stuff is elevated by the work of all of the actors. What matters here is not just what is being said, but the emotions underneath.
reviews.author: Sheila O'Malley

reviews.text: “All of Us Strangers” is a deliberate narrative that will frustrate some viewers who might consider it a languid horror movie and less a moving drama.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Andrew Haigh’s enthralling ghost story concerns a writer (Andrew Scott) coming to terms with a new love (Paul Mescal) and the parents (Claire Foy and Jamie Bell) who died in his childhood. Watch out— Haigh and his four superlative actors will get you good
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers ends up the gentlest of misfires -- melancholy and well-performed, it struggles to transfigure its ideas into the fullness of art.
reviews.author: Zachary Barnes

reviews.text: Although rooted in the specificity of Adam’s grief as an orphaned only child, the film ultimately reveals raw nerves that many queer people have experienced firsthand.
reviews.author: Naveen Kumar

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers will probably make you cry. Maybe even weep. And while there are some twists along the way, it never feels emotionally manipulative or unearned
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: Andrew Haigh’s All of Us Strangers captures the eerie, disorienting and utterly sacred experience of encountering a lost loved one in your dreams.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: It's really well done and really beautifully acted.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: There are so many moments in this movie that are so unforgettable... I'm not completely on board here, but boy, I really love so much of what this movie is doing.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: Andrew Scott is wonderfully crestfallen throughout, but the small amount of light that comes through when he makes certain connections hits just right.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: [T]he film's emotional impact is raw and, in many instances, quite powerful.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Built around wonderfully well-written conversations that draw out painful emotional truths between these four distinct people, the film is about seeing and being seen in a profound sense.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is one of the most remarkable riffs on the ghost story in years, injecting new life into a genre that was always defined by horror and grief.
reviews.author: Hoai-Tran Bui

reviews.text: Explores a love and connection as vast and unknowable as the universe, as deep as infinity, yet as intimate and close and thrilling as the soft touch of bare skin.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: It’s awful to think that this is being sold to gay audiences as a romance, as a chance to fully experience queer love onscreen. Do they think we won’t understand the horror of the final shot?
reviews.author: Sarah Manvel

reviews.text: ... The script does not miss a single opportunity to affirm the ephemeral nature of happiness and the inevitable space of loneliness in the face of emotional wounds. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: Elegiac [and] beautifully filmed.
reviews.author: Mark Leydorf

reviews.text: Remarkably for a film that deals with so much loss, longing and yearning, Haigh has managed a delicate balance. The movie isn’t at all weighed down by sadness. We may be left with mysteries, but the film speaks directly to the importance of love.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is set in Christmastime and brings to the holiday table the spirits of the past and present, some of which are friendly and caring and others distant and ostracizing.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Manages to summon a special level of tenderness during the run time, creating a viewing experience with uncommon intimacy.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: The trouble is that the very conception of All of Us Strangers, with its supernatural hook, is somewhat at odds with Haigh’s general approach to psychological and behavioral credibility.
reviews.author: Lawrence Garcia

reviews.text: Mescal matches Scott look for look, anguish for anguish. But that’s not all they give; there’s also joy in each other and an electric charge to their physical connection. Both are open-hearted performances, fearless in laying bare their sensitive souls.
reviews.author: Murtada Elfadl

reviews.text: Haigh’s uneven metaphysical romance addresses themes of love, grief, loneliness, trauma and memory, but the film provides more ambiguity than insight. Despite a suitably elegiac mood, this film feels undercooked — when it isn’t too on the nose.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: Protagonist Adam (Andrew Scott) lives in a neatly furnished home, no longer feels the need to hide his sexuality, and tells himself he’s fine, but the music says otherwise.
reviews.author: Jennie Kermode

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is an exquisite portrait of a man coping with love and loss.
reviews.author: Joseph Robinson

reviews.text: Conveys the confusion of grief. It stays with you as one tries to reconcile memories with one's new life in which the dead are no longer a part.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: A devastating look at loss and the coming out experience is at the center of director Andrew Haigh’s newest tearjerker.
reviews.author: Matthew Creith

reviews.text: Haigh’s rather metaphysical mise-en-scène is so intricate, and its spellcasting so absolute, that one may be too mesmerized to notice he puts just as much thought into the filmmaking as the emotional tenderness.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Devastation without manipulation.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: It comes so eloquently despite a narrative that leaves us with more mysteries than conclusions – yet still manages to find a triumphant joy – makes it easily one of the best movies of the year.
reviews.author: John Paul King

reviews.text: Scott has the ability to draw you in and hold your attention just with a small vocal inflection or his eyes filled with amazement.
reviews.author: Neely Swanson

reviews.text: "All of Us Strangers" is magical realism...But where the movie excels, it is also hindered. Haigh maintains tension and believability by never varying the movie’s tone, which works but also can make for a trying sit.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers works on so many different levels with Andrew Haigh allowing the audience to interpret this with whatever lens and personal history they bring to it.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: It’s a strange, poetic film that, in the protagonist’s helplessness with regard to his parents, brings up some of the same emotions as in “Hamlet.”
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: In the best way, All of Us Strangers is devastating. The sort of simple-on-paper film that packs an absolute emotional wallop, a true gift of a film.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Too abstract and messy for the most part, it’s the film’s haunting, deeply moving, and profound final act that truly makes it an outstanding piece of cinema.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Paul Mescal gives a performance to equal his portrayal of a damaged dad in Aftersun.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: Paradoxically devastating yet detached, All of Us Strangers’ narrative hook and cast make for a solid watch, but the stylistic and directorial shortcomings rob the film of maximum emotional potential.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: Paul Mescal and Andrew Scott spark in a masterful love story of loneliness and healing.
reviews.author: Anna Bogutskaya

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is a poignantly refined mosaic that encapsulates the terrors and aches of loneliness with a superbly gifted cast who embody some of the most challenging human emotions with immense heart and vulnerability.
reviews.author: Gissane Sophia

reviews.text: Taichi Yamada’s Strangers originally features a straight protagonist, but the book’s themes of loneliness and an unhappy childhood lend themselves to a queer interpretation.
reviews.author: Li Lai

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is a beautiful movie all around, with beautiful imagery, beautiful dialogue, and beautiful relationships.
reviews.author: Jason Flatt

reviews.text: This striking, beautiful, unfairly tragic film is a haunting lullaby that may speak to a certain audience specifically and profoundly, but should prove universally affecting all the same.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Director Andrew Haigh created an environment in which Andrew Scott, Paul Mescal, Claire Foy, and Jamie Bell delivered solid work. But the film feels lacking.
reviews.author: Mike Shutt

reviews.text: It’s evident that Andrew Haigh is a skilled, stylized film director who adeptly realizes the stories he envisions and crafts them to fit his unique vision.
reviews.author: Tyler Strandberg

reviews.text: It’s a really extraordinary film, pretty substantively Haigh’s best.
reviews.author: Scott Nye

reviews.text: The movie leaves a lasting impression and raises profound questions about the human condition. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Matías Mora Montero

reviews.text: A haunting lullaby caught on a breeze carrying the broken glass poetry of Frankie Goes to Hollywood’s ‘The Power of Love’ and the Pet Shop Boys’ Elvis refrain, ‘Always On My Mind’.
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: A deeply moving film about loss and loneliness with a quartet of performances that blend together in a breathtaking way.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: With a moving performance by Andrew Scott, the drama is compelling & captivating as it tackles grief, loneliness & the inability to move on past loss.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: This is a gently involving, darkly personal film that carries a massive emotional wallop.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: The more you think about what you’ve seen, the more the visions resonate. Long after the end credits you’re still left with a haunting feeling.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: This is no gimmicky supernatural thriller; yes, it is a ghost story of sorts, but one about identity and desire, grief, regret, and abandonment, as well as the longing for connection – with queerness at its center.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is working on multiple levels with its seemingly simple concept beautifully executed. It shows its central character exploring his need to confront grief, move on with his life and chase love.
reviews.author: Katherine McLaughlin

reviews.text: Filmmaker Andrew Haigh strikes gold in this moving, heart-wrenching drama about the lasting trauma of grief, isolation and the all-too-human fear of loneliness.
reviews.author: Laura Babiak

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is a gut-wrenching reflection on grief that will leave few dry eyes in cinemas. It is another triumphant film for Andrew Haigh and makes the most of its cast who are all spot on.
reviews.author: Christopher Connor

reviews.text: It’s a film about grief and loneliness, and it leaves you with less of both.
reviews.author: Emily Wheeler

reviews.text: You’ve likely never seen a movie that tackles the specific loneliness many gay men still face today, and this one is laudable for that alone. However, All of Us Strangers airs on the side of saccharine, especially towards the end.
reviews.author: Lena Wilson

reviews.text: I’ve not cried as much at a film as I did with this one. It’s such a tender and carefully told tale of loneliness, of love and loss and longing.
reviews.author: Charlotte Harrison

reviews.text: The best adaptations are often not the most faithful, but those that take the essence of a scenario and employ it for an entirely different agenda. That’s the case with Andrew Haigh’s mysterious and heartbreakingly tender All Of Us Strangers.
reviews.author: Demetrios Matheou

reviews.text: With All of Us Strangers (2023) Haigh returns to the most intimate and melancholic portrait of a contemporary homosexual experience similar to Weekend... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gustavo Herrera Taboada

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is a film that becomes all the more haunting the further from it you get.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is a gut-wrenching reflection on grief that will leave few dry eyes in cinemas. It is another triumphant film for Andrew Haigh and ranks among the year’s best.
reviews.author: Chris Connor

reviews.text: We may all be strangers heading in but by the close of this devastatingly beautiful masterclass from director Andrew Haigh. Audiences will feel united in the collective catharsis experienced.
reviews.author: Darryl Griffiths

reviews.text: All Of Us Strangers reflects on one's past while examining an individual's inability to move forward from loss and trauma.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: Haigh, loosely adapting a 1987 novel by the recently deceased Japanese writer Taichi Yamada, layers so much meaning and feeling into the film it never once plays like a message movie. Instead it’s a ghost story in the best sense – evocative and haunting.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: ... This film admirably sits amid Andrew Haigh’s honourable portfolio of taking sexuality seriously.
reviews.author: Paul Flynn

reviews.text: It shimmers, and it aches.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: All Of Us Strangers that enter the cinema to watch this film, will find themselves bonded from that shared experience of witnessing a truly stunning piece of filmmaking and storytelling.
reviews.author: Dallas King

reviews.text: Haigh seems to confirm that the only people who can understand that kind of grief are those who have experienced it, and who are just as broken as we are and therefore unable to fix us. But it’s also what makes the film so strangely comforting.
reviews.author: Serena Seghedoni

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is a haunting and entirely relatable musing on grief and the bond between a child and their parents, regardless of any separation of time and age, that will drag out your own emotional reaction to the story as the credits roll.
reviews.author: Tori Brazier

reviews.text: Andrew Haigh explores childhood trauma and the protagonist’s complex grieving process through countless memorably powerful, thought-provoking dialogues, performed brilliantly by the entire cast, especially Andrew Scott.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is a quiet but fierce film, cutting right to the center of how grief becomes part of a human’s life.
reviews.author: Emma Kiely

reviews.text: So sure is Haigh’s touch that All of Us Strangers survives a closing audiovisual flourish that asks a lot of even the most indulgent audiences. Only a heel would object.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Two of Ireland’s brightest screen stars are paired to fine effect in the achingly melancholic All of Us Strangers.
reviews.author: Raphael Abraham

reviews.text: Touches the heart.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Andrew Haigh’s All of Us Strangers is a devastating, profound look at how we desperately hold onto the people and memories that link us to our pasts.
reviews.author: Kaveh Jalinous

reviews.text: Despite its deflating ending, it remains a moving example of how cinema can fold tragedy and catharsis into one. It is, after all, a medium of ghosts reflected to us from the past, a notion which Haigh leans into without hesitation or apology.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: A lot of movies attempt to replicate the experience of a dream; this one situates itself right on the edge, whether ecstatic or delirious or stricken, of waking up.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: Even in its overwhelming melancholic power, Haigh has made something therapeutic—about longing and holding on and learning to let go. They’re human lessons that sometimes need a paranormal push.
reviews.author: Jake Kring-Schreifels

reviews.text: By sacrificing the restraint he typically wields so skillfully, Haigh keeps the film from being truly great.
reviews.author: Stephanie Monohan

reviews.text: Haigh is a master of his craft, and All of Us Strangers is a must-see masterpiece of storytelling. It shook me to my core, and I hope it does the same for all of you strangers.
reviews.author: Jonathan Sim

reviews.text: Sad Boy Cinema gains a crowning jewel with Andrew Haigh’s devastating and deeply felt All of Us Strangers... an epic of intimacy with a staggering open wound of a performance from Andrew Scott in its lead
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is a love story and a tragedy, a fantasy and a horror film, a drama and a sexy romance--sexy and doomed.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: Emotional and lyrical, All of Us Strangers is a meditation on what it means to really be a human.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is literally a haunting meditation on grief over the death of loved ones. This well-acted drama might be too slow-paced for some viewers, but the movie's themes and performances are worth watching. Some of it gets repetitive though.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: This is a movie that savors.
reviews.author: Rich Juzwiak

reviews.text: [Andrew] Haigh crafts his most accessible film yet, a tender treatise on the undying power of love and what happens when we ignore its force.
reviews.author: Coleman Spilde

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers refuses to indulge an “it gets better” fantasy by pretending contemporary urban spaces and millennial openness are signs of inevitable progress.
reviews.author: Marshall Shaffer

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers sublimely addresses honest truths long hidden in the shadows. Death's cruel finality leaves a gaping void in the lives of those left behind. Your heart will soar and break in a powerfully emotional journey of devastating loss.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Writer-director Andrew Haigh’s moody, devastating supernatural love story juxtaposes queer past with queer present, muddying the answer in ways that feel as true as they do pessimistic.
reviews.author: Matthew Dougherty

reviews.text: Haigh more than furthered himself, and the growing canon of queer fantastical films has gained one of its most important entries to date.
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: Scott is extraordinary in what is easily his best role to date, quietly gathering a growing force that provides the film with one last emotional wallop that will move any audience to tears.
reviews.author: Tom O'Brien

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is a magnificent portrait of loneliness and retrospective identity that penetrates deep into the soul. It’s one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: [A] monotonous experience with a hokey finish.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Like 45 Years, Haigh knows how to close a film and the final shot of All of Us Strangers will be a part of me forever. Haigh has created a timeless masterpiece and one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Erik Anderson

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers will break your heart — but it just might mend it too.
reviews.author: Maureen Lee Lenker

reviews.text: Andrew Haigh has reached new heights and crafted something utterly and profoundly beautiful... an intimate and sensitive exploration of the connections we forge in life and the inevitable need to let go and move forward from them in various ways
reviews.author: Mark Johnson

reviews.text: All of Us Strangers is a deeply moving and personal work that will mean different things to different people.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: This is Scott’s film, though. His performance is intelligent and quietly moving, and he deserves more meaty leading roles like this.
reviews.author: Ed Potton

reviews.text: A sublime masterpiece. A rumination on grief and love, Haigh’s poignant and understated ghost story is one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: Andrew Haigh stuns with a hard-to-categorise drama that's both fantastical and engagingly grounded. Ace performances all round.
reviews.author: Matt Maytum

reviews.text: Despite the actor’s excellent contributions, this is still the work of a confident auteur. Andrew Haigh has many skills as a director and letting the action play out subtle manner is one of them.
reviews.author: Gregory Ellwood

reviews.text: Prepare to be wrecked.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: “All of Us Strangers” is therapy for the audience, or at least that specific segment of us who desperately need to hear our fathers say, “I’m sorry I never came in your room when you were crying.”
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: A supernova of a film; Haigh is a modern master.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: A luxuriantly sad and skin-tinglingly sensual gay romance, it is propelled by a killer combination of 80s queer pop and a pair of devastating performances from Scott and Mescal.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: An enormously satisfying and affecting experience.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Haigh, whose less is more approach has never been more effective than it is here, always makes sure to leave room in the frame for us to bring our own hurt to the table, whatever form it might take.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Older viewers may run headlong toward the film’s despondency, finding solace, even catharsis, in its haunting ache. It’s a difficult work, raggedly emotional but chilly.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: It is a challenging work as much of Haigh’s character-driven filmography including Weekend and 45 Years often is, but one that offers rich rewards if you sign on to it at all.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

synopsis: One night in his near-empty tower block in contemporary London, Adam (Andrew Scott) has a chance encounter with a mysterious neighbor Harry (Paul Mescal), which punctures the rhythm of his everyday life. As a relationship develops between them, Adam is preoccupied with memories of the past and finds himself drawn back to the suburban town where he grew up, and the childhood home where his parents (Claire Foy and Jamie Bell), appear to be living, just as they were on the day they died, 30 years before.
